title: Nystrom product integration and fredholm error

items.title: Nyström quadrature operators and their reconstructed equations
items.statement: Let $X:=C([0,1],\mathbb R)$ be the real continuous functions on $[0,1]$ ([[def-continuous-real-functions-on-a-compact-metric-space]]) with the supremum norm $\|u\|_\infty:=\sup_{0\le x\le1}|u(x)|$; this is a Banach space by [[thm-c-k-complete-in-the-sup-metric]]. Fix a continuous real kernel $k:[0,1]^2\to\mathbb R$. The integral $\int_0^1$ below is the ordinary Riemann integral, equivalently the Riemann–Stieltjes integral with integrator $y\mapsto y$ ([[def-riemann-stieltjes-sum-and-integral]]). For $u\in X$, define $$ (Ku)(x):=\int_0^1 k(x,y)u(y)\,dy,\qquad 0\le x\le1. $$ The integrand is continuous in $y$, so this integral exists by [[thm-continuous-implies-integrable]]. A finite quadrature rule on $[0,1]$ consists of an integer $m\ge1$, nodes $y_1,\ldots,y_m\in[0,1]$, and real weights $w_1,\ldots,w_m$. It acts on a function $g$ defined at the nodes by $$Q(g):=\sum_{j=1}^m w_jg(y_j).$$ Its Nyström operator is the finite-sum rule $$ (K_Q u)(x):=Q\bigl(k(x,\cdot)u(\cdot)\bigr) =\sum_{j=1}^m w_jk(x,y_j)u(y_j). $$ In particular, for the composite midpoint rule with $N\ge1$ panels, $h:=1/N$, $y_j:=(j+\tfrac12)h$ for $0\le j<N$, and $w_j=h$, the operator is denoted $K_N$. The nodes and weights are those of [[alg-composite-midpoint-rule]]. For a right-hand side $f\in X$, the Nyström equation is $$u_Q-K_Qu_Q=f.$$ This definition asserts neither consistency nor convergence of $K_Q$ to $K$.

items.title: Finite-node Nyström equations are equivalent to their reconstructed equations
items.statement: Let $X:=C([0,1],\mathbb R)$ ([[def-continuous-real-functions-on-a-compact-metric-space]]), let $m\ge1$, let $y_1,\ldots,y_m\in[0,1]$, and let $\psi_1,\ldots,\psi_m\in X$. Define the finite-rank linear map $$ (Fu)(x):=\sum_{j=1}^m\psi_j(x)u(y_j) $$ and, for $f\in X$, define the square matrix and vector $$ M_{ij}:=\delta_{ij}-\psi_j(y_i),\qquad b_i:=f(y_i),\qquad 1\le i,j\le m. $$ Then the solutions of $(I-F)u=f$ are in bijection with the solutions $c\in\mathbb R^m$ of $Mc=b$, via $$u(x)=f(x)+\sum_{j=1}^m\psi_j(x)c_j,\qquad c_i=u(y_i).$$ The nullspaces of $I-F$ and $M$ are linearly isomorphic by $c\mapsto\sum_j\psi_jc_j$. In particular, $I-F$ is bijective if and only if $M$ is nonsingular.

items.title: A continuous kernel defines a compact integral operator on C of an interval
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice. Let $X:=C([0,1],\mathbb R)$ with $\|u\|_\infty:=\sup_{x\in[0,1]}|u(x)|$ ([[def-continuous-real-functions-on-a-compact-metric-space]], [[thm-c-k-complete-in-the-sup-metric]]) and let $k:[0,1]^2\to\mathbb R$ be continuous. The map $$ (Ku)(x):=\int_0^1 k(x,y)u(y)\,dy $$ uses the ordinary Riemann integral of [[def-riemann-stieltjes-sum-and-integral]] and defines a bounded linear operator $K:X\to X$, and it is compact ([[def-compact-linear-operator]]).

items.title: Collective compactness gives eventual Fredholm invertibility and solution error bounds
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $X\ne\{0\}$ be a Banach space ([[def-banach-space]]), let $K:X\to X$ be compact, and let $(K_n)_{n\ge1}$ be bounded linear operators such that $$\overline{\bigcup_{n\ge1}K_n(B_X)}$$ is compact for the closed unit ball $B_X:=\{x\in X:\|x\|\le1\}$ and $K_nx\to Kx$ in norm for every $x\in X$. Suppose $I-K$ is injective. Then there are $n_0\ge1$ and $C<\infty$ such that $I-K_n$ is boundedly invertible for every $n\ge n_0$ and $$\sup_{n\ge n_0}\|(I-K_n)^{-1}\|\le C.$$ For any $f,f_n\in X$, if $u$ and $u_n$ solve $(I-K)u=f$ and $(I-K_n)u_n=f_n$, then for $n\ge n_0$, $$\|u_n-u\|\le C\bigl(\|(K_n-K)u\|+\|f_n-f\|\bigr).$$ The theorem does not assert that $\|K_n-K\|\to0$.

items.title: The half-order diagonal singularity defines a bounded improper integral
items.statement: For $x\in[0,1]$, $g\in C([0,1],\mathbb R)$, and $0<\varepsilon<1$, let $$S_{x,\varepsilon}(g):=\int_{[0,1]\setminus(x-\varepsilon,x+\varepsilon)}|x-y|^{-1/2}g(y)\,dy,$$ where the integral is the sum of the ordinary Riemann integrals on the at most two remaining closed intervals, and an empty interval contributes zero. The limit $$S_x(g):=\lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}S_{x,\varepsilon}(g)$$ exists. The map $S_x:C([0,1],\mathbb R)\to\mathbb R$ is linear and positive, and its operator norm ([[def-operator-norm]]) is $$\|S_x\|=S_x(1)=2\sqrt{x}+2\sqrt{1-x}\le2\sqrt2.$$

items.title: Translations of the half-order kernel are continuous in the improper L1 norm
items.statement: Put $s(t):=|t|^{-1/2}$ for $t\in[-1,1]\setminus\{0\}$. For $x,x'\in[0,1]$, define $$T(x,x'):=\int_0^1|s(x-y)-s(x'-y)|\,dy$$ as an improper Riemann integral split at the distinct points among $x$ and $x'$; an endpoint value at a singular point is omitted. If $x=x'$, set $T(x,x)=0$. These improper integrals exist and are finite. The modulus $$\tau(d):=\sup\{T(x,x'):x,x'\in[0,1],\ |x-x'|\le d\}$$ is finite and satisfies $\tau(d)\to0$ as $d\downarrow0$.

items.title: The operator-norm Nyström perturbation bound
items.statement: Use $X$, $K$, and the finite quadrature Nyström operator $K_Q$ from [[def-nystrom-quadrature-and-finite-rank-operators]]. Suppose $A:=I-K$ has a bounded inverse, put $R:=\|A^{-1}\|$, and let $\varepsilon:=\|K_Q-K\|$ as an operator on $X$. If $q:=R\varepsilon<1$, then $I-K_Q$ has a bounded inverse and $$\|(I-K_Q)^{-1}\|\le\frac{R}{1-q}.$$ For $f,f_Q\in X$, let $u$ and $u_Q$ solve $(I-K)u=f$ and $(I-K_Q)u_Q=f_Q$. Then $$\|u_Q-u\|_\infty\le\frac{R}{1-q} \bigl(\|(K_Q-K)u\|_\infty+\|f_Q-f\|_\infty\bigr).$$ When $Q$ is point sampling on all of $C([0,1],\mathbb R)$, this theorem is conditional: its hypothesis is an actual operator-norm bound, not merely convergence of the quadrature on each fixed continuous integrand.

items.title: Composite midpoint Nyström operators are collectively compact and consistent
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $k:[0,1]^2\to\mathbb R$ be continuous and let $K$ be its integral operator from [[def-nystrom-quadrature-and-finite-rank-operators]]. For each $N\ge1$, let $K_N$ use the composite midpoint rule with $h=1/N$. Then $K$ is compact, the family $(K_N)_{N\ge1}$ is collectively compact (the union of the images of the unit ball has compact closure in $X$), and $$\|K_Nu-Ku\|_\infty\longrightarrow0\qquad\text{for every }u\in X.$$

items.title: Piecewise-linear product integration for a half-order diagonal singularity
items.statement: Let $X:=C([0,1],\mathbb R)$ and let $a:[0,1]^2\to\mathbb R$ be continuous. Use $S_x$ from [[lem-half-order-singular-integral-exists]] to define $$ (Ku)(x):=S_x\bigl(y\mapsto a(x,y)u(y)\bigr). $$ For an integer $n\ge1$, set $h:=1/n$ and $y_j:=jh$ for $j=0,\ldots,n$. Define the nonnegative piecewise-linear hat functions by $$\phi_{n,0}(y):=\max(1-y/h,0),\qquad \phi_{n,n}(y):=\max(1-(1-y)/h,0),$$ and, for $1\le j<n$, $$\phi_{n,j}(y):=\max(1-|y-y_j|/h,0).$$ Their piecewise-linear interpolant is $$I_ng:=\sum_{j=0}^n g(y_j)\phi_{n,j}.$$ The product weights and product-integration operator are $$w_{n,j}(x):=S_x(\phi_{n,j}),\qquad (K_nu)(x):=\sum_{j=0}^n w_{n,j}(x)a(x,y_j)u(y_j) =S_x\bigl(I_n(y\mapsto a(x,y)u(y))\bigr).$$ The kernel factor $s(x,y)=|x-y|^{-1/2}$ is integrated in the weights; the smooth factor $a(x,y)u(y)$ is interpolated. This item defines the pointwise formulas; the subsequent results on this page establish their mapping properties, stability, and error estimates.

items.title: Closed forms for the half-order piecewise-linear product weights
items.statement: Use the nodes, hats, and weights $w_{n,j}(x)=S_x(\phi_{n,j})$ of [[def-half-order-product-integration]]. For $x\in[0,1]$, $0\le\alpha\le\beta\le1$, and $u,v\in\mathbb R$, put $C:=u+vx$ and, for $r\ge0$, define $$P_{x,u,v}(r):=2C\sqrt r+\frac23v r\sqrt r,\qquad Q_{x,u,v}(r):=2C\sqrt r-\frac23v r\sqrt r.$$ Write $r_+:=\max(r,0)$ and set $$\mathcal J_x[\alpha,\beta;u,v]:= Q_{x,u,v}((x-\alpha)_+)-Q_{x,u,v}((x-\beta)_+) +P_{x,u,v}((\beta-x)_+)-P_{x,u,v}((\alpha-x)_+).$$ Then this is the exact improper Riemann integral $$\mathcal J_x[\alpha,\beta;u,v] =\int_\alpha^\beta |x-y|^{-1/2}(u+vy)\,dy,$$ with the integral split at $x$ if $x\in[\alpha,\beta]$. In particular, for $h=1/n$ and $y_j=jh$, $$w_{n,0}(x)=\mathcal J_x[0,h;1,-h^{-1}],$$ $$w_{n,j}(x)=\mathcal J_x[y_{j-1},y_j;-y_{j-1}/h,h^{-1}] +\mathcal J_x[y_j,y_{j+1};y_{j+1}/h,-h^{-1}],\quad 1\le j<n,$$ and $$w_{n,n}(x)=\mathcal J_x[y_{n-1},1;-y_{n-1}/h,h^{-1}].$$ The formulas include $x$ at a panel endpoint and the one-panel case $n=1$.

items.title: Smooth-solution error bound for composite midpoint Nyström discretization
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $k:[0,1]^2\to\mathbb R$ be continuous, $K$ its integral operator, and $K_N$ its composite midpoint Nyström operator with panel width $h=1/N$. Suppose $I-K$ is injective and $u$ solves $(I-K)u=f$. Assume that $g_x(y):=k(x,y)u(y)$ is twice continuously differentiable in $y$ for every $x$, with the uniform bound $$M_2:=\sup_{x,y\in[0,1]}|\partial_y^2g_x(y)|<\infty.$$ Then there are $N_0$ and $C<\infty$ such that for every $N\ge N_0$ the Nyström matrix is nonsingular, its reconstruction $u_N$ solving $(I-K_N)u_N=f_N$ exists for each $f_N\in X$, and $$\|u_N-u\|_\infty\le C\left(\|f_N-f\|_\infty+\frac{h^2}{24}M_2\right).$$ In the standard Nyström method $f_N=f$. The regularity assumption is on the actual function $k(x,\cdot)u(\cdot)$, not on every function in the unit ball of $C([0,1],\mathbb R)$.

items.title: Stability, collective compactness, and consistency of half-order product integration
items.statement: Assume AC and let $a:[0,1]^2\to\mathbb R$ be continuous. For $K$ and $K_n$ from [[def-half-order-product-integration]], put $A:=\|a\|_\infty$ and $h:=1/n$. Then both operators map $X=C([0,1],\mathbb R)$ to itself, $K$ is compact, and $(K_n)$ is collectively compact and converges pointwise in norm to $K$. Their product weights satisfy $$w_{n,j}(x)\ge0,\qquad \sum_{j=0}^n|w_{n,j}(x)| =2\sqrt{x}+2\sqrt{1-x}\le2\sqrt2$$ for every $x\in[0,1]$. If each $g_x(y):=a(x,y)u(y)$ extends to a $C^2$ function on a neighborhood of $[0,1]$ and $M_2:=\sup_{x,y}|\partial_y^2g_x(y)|<\infty$, then $$\|K_nu-Ku\|_\infty\le\frac{\sqrt2}{4}M_2h^2.$$

items.title: Fredholm error bound for half-order product integration
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $a:[0,1]^2\to\mathbb R$ be continuous, let $K,K_n$ be the half-order product-integration operators of [[def-half-order-product-integration]], and suppose $I-K$ is injective. Let $u$ solve $(I-K)u=f$, and assume each $g_x(y):=a(x,y)u(y)$ extends to a $C^2$ function on a neighborhood of $[0,1]$, with $$M_2:=\sup_{x,y\in[0,1]}|\partial_y^2(a(x,y)u(y))|<\infty.$$ Then there are $n_0$ and $C<\infty$ such that for every $n\ge n_0$, the finite Nyström grid matrix is nonsingular, its reconstructed solution $u_n$ exists, and $$\|u_n-u\|_\infty\le C\left(\|f_n-f\|_\infty+\frac{\sqrt2}{4}M_2h^2\right), \qquad h=1/n,$$ whenever $(I-K_n)u_n=f_n$. In particular, for the exact right-hand side $f_n=f$, the solution error is $O(h^2)$ under the stated smoothness of the regular factor times the exact solution.

title: Nystrom product integration and fredholm error — Examples

items.title: A two-node Gaussian Nyström rule solves a rank-two separable equation exactly
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. Let $\mu$ be Lebesgue measure on $[0,1]$, take $\alpha=1/4$, $\beta=1/2$, and set $k(x,y)=\alpha+\beta xy$ and $f(x)=1$. The equation $$u(x)-\int_{[0,1]}k(x,y)u(y)\,d\mu(y)=1$$ has the unique solution $$u(x)=\frac{80+24x}{57}.$$ The two-node Gaussian rule for $\mu$ gives the exact same solution and a nonsingular two-by-two grid system. The continuous integrals can equivalently be read as Riemann integrals under Countable Choice.

items.title: A near-resonant Nyström equation amplifies midpoint quadrature error
items.statement: For $0<\delta<1$, set $\lambda:=3(1-\delta)$, define $$ (Ku)(x):=\lambda x\int_0^1 yu(y)\,dy,$$ and let $f(x)=1$. The exact solution of $u-Ku=f$ is $$u(x)=1+\frac{\lambda}{2\delta}x.$$ For the $N$-panel composite midpoint rule with $h=1/N$, the Nyström solution is $$u_N(x)=1+\frac{\lambda}{2(\delta+\lambda h^2/12)}x.$$ Its error is the midpoint residual multiplied by a factor $$(\delta+\lambda h^2/12)^{-1},$$ which is at least $(2\delta)^{-1}$ whenever $\lambda h^2/12\le\delta$. Thus a small quadrature residual can produce a much larger solution error as $\delta$ approaches the resonance value $0$.

items.title: Direct midpoint quadrature loses order on a half-order singularity
items.statement: At $x=0$, take the weakly singular kernel $s(0,y)=y^{-1/2}$ and smooth factor $a\equiv1$, $u\equiv1$. The exact integral is $2$. The composite midpoint rule on panels of width $h=1/N$ underestimates it by at least $$(2-\sqrt2)\sqrt h,$$ so direct midpoint sampling of this singular integrand is not second order. The product-integration rule of [[def-half-order-product-integration]] is exact for this constant smooth factor, because its interpolant is identically $1$.
